After having a horrible experience with Robert Darbishire Practice, I registered with Dr. Ngan and Partners in February 2023. At first, I was very impressed with how quickly I was able to get appointments with the doctors. However, things quickly took a turn for the worse.

1. A severe and persistent headache started on 2nd February 2023 and lasted for the whole of the month. This headache did not subside with any medications, even those for migraines. I then had two telephonic consultations with Dr. Ngan and Partners during which time the doctor agreed that it was probably a sinus headache and not a migraine. He prescribed sinus related medications both times, but the pain did not reduce. By this time three weeks had passed since the headache had started. I informed the doctor that the pain was excruciating and had me bedridden most of the time. I also requested the doctor for an MRI or CT scan during the second consultation but this request was denied. I was also not referred to a neurologist or an ENT specialist despite the nature, duration and intensity of the headache.
2. I also informed the doctor that I had visited the ER earlier in the month as the pain worsened but could not see the doctor due to the long waiting time, hoping this would convey how severe the headache gets sometimes.
3. I contacted Dr. Ngan and Partners for the third time on 24th February and got an in-person appointment for the same day. After conducting physical examinations, the doctor diagnosed it as a migraine and prescribed a migraine medication AGAIN, even after I told her that literally no medications were working. I requested for an MRI or CT scan referral twice during the consultation but my request was denied for the third time! She said "there is nothing specific that we are looking for that would turn up in the scans". Instead, she said she would refer me to a neurologist if the headache persisted for a few more days. By this time, it was the start of the 4th week since the headache had started.
4. On 26th February 2023, I had to call an ambulance as the pain exponentially increased, so much so that I felt like my right eye was about to pop out! I had fever and vomiting. I was told that because my vitals, etc., were normal, they will not be able to take me to the ER. I called Dr. Ngan on 27th hysterically crying and explained my situation. I requested for an urgent consultation with the doctor but was told that there was no possibility of getting an appointment that day or the next as all slots were full.
5. I told the doctors that I was first on Co-codamol as prescribed by the previous GP but the intensity reduced. I was then asked to use Ibuprofen during first consultation with Dr. Ngan. During the last consultation I told the doctor that I had been on Ibuprofen for 10 days straight but she still asked me to use it to control pain.
5. Having felt completely and utterly abandoned by the GP, I had to fly home, to India, on 28th to receive urgent medical treatment.  It was a gruelling 22 hours of travel during which the pain almost killed me! Upon investigation after getting admitted in India, it was found that I had a rare and an extremely severe infection in the Sphenoid sinus. The scans revealed that the infection had progressed so much that if I had waited for a few more days to get treated, I would have lost vision in my right eye or suffered brain damage! The infection had broken down the wall between the sinus and the brain and had started seeping into the brain, and the only way out was to have an immediate surgery. I was also told that the constant use of the painkillers prescribed by the GP was the reason why I had started puking blood on 28th February.
6. PATIENT HISTORY MATTERS! I had told the GP that I had suffered a scuba diving injury in 2020 after which I suffered similar headaches. However, this was completely ignored.
